The DSSSB Assistant Superintendent Result 2026 has been released for the Assistant Superintendent post in Delhi Prisons under Post Code 32/25. Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board issued Result Notice No. 204 (Tier-I) on 5 October 2026. A total of 932 candidates have been provisionally shortlisted for the Physical Endurance Test (PET). 

The Tier-I online examination was conducted in different shifts from 1 July to 7 July 2026. DSSSB has uploaded the marks of 22,258 candidates who appeared in the examination. Candidates can check their individual marks by logging into the OARS module

  1. Visit the DSSSB official website at dsssb.delhi.gov.in.

  6. For individual marks, visit the DSSSB OARS portal.

Also Read: Rajasthan SET Answer Key 2026

DSSSB Assistant Superintendent Exam Date 2026

The online Tier-I written examination for Assistant Superintendent was conducted in different shifts from 1 July to 7 July 2026. The result was subsequently declared on 5 October 2026.

Event Date
Advertisement 31 July 2025

DSSSB Assistant Superintendent Minimum Qualifying Marks

According to the DSSSB result notice, the minimum qualifying marks for a one-tier written examination are 40% for UR and EWS, 35% for OBC and 30% for SC, ST and PwBD candidates. Ex-servicemen receive 5% relaxation in their respective categories, subject to a minimum of 30%. 

These minimum qualifying percentages are different from the category-wise PET shortlisting cut-offs shown above.

What Happens After DSSSB Assistant Superintendent Result 2026?

The next stage is the Physical Endurance Test (PET). DSSSB has stated that PET details will be notified separately. Candidates shortlisted in the Tier-I result should regularly check the Board's website for the PET schedule and related instructions.

Shortlisting for PET does not by itself give a candidate a right to appointment. DSSSB has not yet completed detailed scrutiny of eligibility documents for the shortlisted candidates.

Is DSSSB Assistant Superintendent Result 2026 Final?

No. The result released on 5 October 2026 is a Tier-I provisional result for shortlisting candidates to the Physical Endurance Test. Candidates must complete the subsequent recruitment stages before final selection.

The Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS) published a tentative merit list for administrative posts under the TIMS recruitment on 3 October 2026. Candidates on the list have been called for verification of certificates. The date, time and venue of verification are not available in the information checked for this article, so confirm them in the official PDF.

Direct link to check NIMS Administrative and Support Service Merit List 2026

NIMS Tentative Merit List 2026 - Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Recruiting organisation Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Hyderabad
Institute for which posts are filled Telangana Institute of Medical Sciences (TIMS), Sanath Nagar
Posts covered Administrative and Support Service
Merit list release date 3 October 2026
Official Website nims.edu.in

What Does a Tentative Merit List Mean?

A tentative merit list is a provisional ranking of candidates. It can change after certificates are checked, for example if a document is missing or does not match the eligibility conditions. This is general information about how such lists work. The exact rules for this list are in the official PDF.

Important Dates

Event Date
Tentative merit list released 3 October 2026

How to Check the NIMS Tentative Merit List

  1. Open the NIMS current recruitment page.
  2. Find the entry titled "NIMS -Recruitment of Administrative Posts - Tentative Merit List Called For Verification of Certificates".
  3. Open the linked PDF, or go directly to the NIMS merit list PDF.
  4. Search for your name or application details in the list.
  5. Read any instructions printed in the PDF about verification and follow them exactly.

Also Read: RRB Ministerial & Isolated Category Result 2026

Documents Required for Certificate Verification

The document list for verification is not available in the information checked. Use the official PDF as the final authority.

The original application instructions, as reported by job portals, asked for self-attested copies of the following. Keep the originals of these ready in case they are requested:

  • Date of birth proof
  • Educational qualification certificates
  • Experience certificates
  • Registration certificates, where applicable
  • Caste, EWS or PwD certificate, where applicable
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC), where applicable
  • Other supporting documents mentioned in the notification

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Read the full merit list PDF before planning your visit.
  • Check that your name, category and details are correct.
  • Carry original documents along with self-attested copies if the notice asks for them.
  • Do not rely on social media posts or unofficial pages for dates and venues. Use the NIMS website.

394 RPSC Veterinary Officer Results Kept in Sealed Cover

The results of 394 candidates have been kept in sealed cover due to pending petitions before the Rajasthan High Court. The cases are connected with proceedings before the Jaipur and Jodhpur benches, and the status of these candidates will remain subject to further court orders. 

Candidates affected by these cases should check the relevant result notice carefully rather than assuming that absence from the Main or Reserve List means a final rejection.

Also Read: HPSC ADO Result 2026

What Does M Number Mean in RPSC Veterinary Officer Merit List?

The letter M identifies a candidate's position in the Main Merit List. For example, M-1 represents the first merit position and M-1100 represents the 1,100th merit position in the Main List.

The letter R is used for Reserve List positions. The Reserve List runs from R-1 to R-455.

What Happens After RPSC Veterinary Officer Main Merit List?

The Main Merit List has been issued after eligibility checking and document verification. Candidates included in the Main List should now follow further appointment-related instructions issued by the concerned Animal Husbandry Department or RPSC. 

No confirmed appointment or joining date is provided in the current merit-list information. Candidates should therefore wait for the relevant departmental notice instead of assuming a joining schedule.

The available Civil score document is headed Andhra Pradesh Vidyut Recruitment-2026 and lists the serial number, hall ticket number, candidate name and score. The other four engineering disciplines are also provided as separate score documents. 

What Does the AP Vidyut Result PDF Contain?

The stream-wise score documents allow candidates to check their individual CBT performance. The documents include the following information:

  • Hall Ticket Number
  • Candidate Name
  • Engineering Discipline
  • CBT Score

The score document states that the scores of candidates who appeared in the APVR-2026 Computer Based Test have been declared. It also clearly says that publication of a score does not by itself confer any right to selection or appointment. 

How to Check AP Vidyut Result 2026

  1. Visit the AP Vidyut recruitment portal at apvidyutrecruitment.apcfss.in.

  6. Check the score shown against your details.
  7. Save a copy of the score document for future reference.

The result reports state that stream-wise scores can be accessed through the AP Vidyut recruitment portal. 

AP Vidyut Score Normalisation 2026

The APVR-2026 score document states that scores have been normalised across different shifts wherever applicable. Normalisation is relevant where candidates appeared in examination shifts with different question papers or difficulty levels.

Candidates should therefore refer to the published score rather than attempting to compare raw performance between different examination shifts.

Is AP Vidyut Score the Final Selection Result?

No. The published APVR-2026 score document specifically states that publication of a score does not give a candidate any right to selection or appointment. Selection is to be made according to merit, reservation rules, eligibility criteria, candidate preferences and certificate verification as prescribed for the recruitment. 

Therefore, candidates should distinguish between the CBT score/result and the eventual selection or appointment outcome.

Certificate verification is identified as an important subsequent part of the recruitment process. The score document states that selection will take into account merit, the Rule of Reservation, eligibility conditions, candidate preferences and certificate verification.

KSRP Police Constable Score List PDF

KEA has published provisional score lists as PDF files, along with a result notice. The lists show application numbers and the marks obtained. Candidates can also see their own marks by logging in on the KEA result page for their cadre.

How to Check KSRP Police Constable Result 2026

Follow these steps to check and download your result:

  1. Visit the official KEA website at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea.
  2. Click the link for the provisional KSRP posts 2026 examination result.
  3. Choose the correct cadre page: RPC or KK.
  4. Enter your application number and date of birth.
  5. Click Submit. Your marks will appear on the screen.
  6. Download the result and keep a printout.

How to Download the KSRP Police Constable Score List PDF

Open the score list PDF for your cadre from the links above. Press Ctrl+F (or use Find on mobile) and enter your application number to jump to your entry.

If any detail looks wrong, note it down and refer to KEA's official notices for the correct way to raise it. The window for objections to the provisional result closed on 27 September 2026.

KEA has not officially released cut-off marks or qualifying marks for the KSRP Police Constable exam. The provisional result shows only the marks obtained. Cut-off details, if any, will be known only when KEA publishes them on its official website.

  1. Check that your name, category and marks are correct.

  4. Start preparing for the Physical Standard Test (PST) and Physical Endurance Test (PET).

  • Follow the invigilators' instructions at all times.

Who Can Appear in the AP Special TET 2026?

The Special TET is only for eligible in-service teachers. Teachers working in the following institutions can appear if they meet the qualification requirements for the paper:

  • Government Welfare Residential Schools
  • AP Model Schools

Each paper has 150 multiple-choice questions for 150 marks. The duration is 2 hours 30 minutes and there is no negative marking.

Candidates should carefully read the instructions printed on their individual call letter because document requirements may vary.

On this page ▾
Overview Dates Centre-wise Vacancies Domain Areas Pay & Age Grades Eligibility Age Relaxation Selection Process How to Apply Important Conditions Important Links

C-DAC Recruitment 2026 Overview

Particulars Details
Organization Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), a Scientific Society of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
Recruitment Cycle JIT (Just-In-Time) October 2026 Cycle
Participating Centres Guwahati (CINE), Thiruvananthapuram, Pune, Noida, Mumbai, Mohali, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Delhi, Chennai, Bengaluru
Approximate Total Posts 844 across all centres combined (see centre-wise table below)
Position Levels Project Associate, Project Engineer, Senior Project Engineer/Module Lead, Project Manager/Program Manager, Tech Lead, plus support roles (HR/Admin, Finance, Purchase, Technician)
Engagement Basis Purely contractual, on consolidated emoluments, initially for up to 3 years or completion of the project (whichever is earlier)
Application Mode Online only, via careers.cdac.in (each centre has its own listing; a separate application is needed per post applied to)
Note: This is a contractual engagement, not a regular C-DAC appointment. Selected candidates do not derive any right or claim to a regular post in C-DAC, and may be deputed or transferred to any C-DAC project location across India based on organizational requirement.

C-DAC Recruitment 2026 Important Dates

Event Date
Commencement of Online Registration 05 October 2026 (timing varies slightly by centre portal, between 00:00 and 09:00 Hrs)
Last Date for Online Registration 26 October 2026 (closing time varies slightly by centre, generally 18:00–23:59 Hrs)
Written Test / Interview Date Will be communicated later, only by email, to shortlisted candidates
Note: The cut-off date for age and experience is the last date of application submission for the respective centre.

Centre-wise Vacancy Summary

Centre Advt./Reference No. Primary Location Position Categories Approx. Posts
C-DAC Noida CORP/JIT/03/2026-ND Noida 28 ~207

Important: Post counts above are tallied from each centre's published position list and are approximate. C-DAC reserves the right to increase, decrease, or not fill any notified post at its discretion, without prior notice. Always verify exact, current vacancy numbers on the respective centre's official listing before applying.

Domain Areas Covered

Across the 11 centres, C-DAC is hiring for a wide range of technical and non-technical domains, including:

  • Full Stack / Web / Mobile App Development
  • Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning & Data Science
  • VLSI, Embedded Systems & Hardware Design (incl. FPGA, PCB Design)
  • Cyber Security & Cyber Forensics (incl. VAPT)
  • Quantum Computing (Algorithms, Optics & Photonics, Cryogenics)
  • Health Informatics
  • e-Governance & Data Centre / Cloud Operations
  • Blockchain, DevOps & System Architecture
  • Education & Training, Heritage and Language Computing
  • HR/Admin, Finance, Purchase, Director's Office & Support Functions

Illustrative Pay & Age Grades

Exact pay and age limits are specified against each individual post on the centre's listing. The table below (from the Bengaluru notification) illustrates how C-DAC's typical grade structure is set up, as a reference:

Grade Upper Age Limit Typical Experience Initial CTC (Min. Experience)
Project Associate 30 yrs (Fresher) / 45 yrs (Experienced) 0+ years ₹3.6 LPA – ₹5.04 LPA
Project Engineer 30 yrs (Fresher) / 45 yrs (Experienced) 0–4 years ₹4.49 LPA – ₹7.11 LPA
Senior Project Engineer / Project Lead / Module Lead 40 years 4–7 years ₹8.49 LPA – ₹14 LPA
Project Manager / Program Manager / Knowledge Partner 56 years 9–15 years ₹12.63 LPA – ₹22.9 LPA

Candidates with experience higher than the minimum required for a grade will be offered additional increments as per C-DAC policy. Pay figures vary by centre, domain, and specific post — always check the individual post listing for the exact bracket.

Eligibility – Qualification & Experience (Common Rules)

Qualification

  • For all posts, candidates should have qualified from an AICTE/UGC-approved college/institute or recognized university.
  • Where a university follows CGPA/DGPA/OGPA or letter grades, the candidate must submit proof of the percentage equivalent and awarded class, along with the degree certificate.
  • Candidates in their final semester, who will complete the course before appointment, may also apply; if selected, joining is contingent on passing with the required minimum score.

Experience

  • Candidates should apply only if they possess the relevant post-qualification experience sought for the post, where specified.
  • Teaching/research work, non-profit organization experience, and internships/academic project placements are not counted as experience unless specified.
  • Experience certificates from previous/current employers must clearly indicate the period of employment, salary drawn, and post held.
  • C-DAC internal candidates need to have completed at least 2 years' service in C-DAC (as of the notification date) to apply for notified positions.
  • Experience claimed without supporting documents will not be considered and is liable to be rejected.
Important: Meeting the minimum qualification and experience does not automatically entitle a candidate to a written test, skill test, or interview call. C-DAC may restrict the number of candidates called, based on qualifications and experience higher than the minimum prescribed.

Age Limit & Relaxation

  • The upper age limit is specified against each individual post (see the Pay & Age Grades table above for typical ranges).
  • SC/ST/OBC, physically challenged (PwBD), and Ex-Servicemen candidates are eligible for age relaxation as per Government of India norms.
  • Government employees on a pay scale get a 5-year age relaxation, in addition to other applicable relaxations.
  • The cut-off date for age and experience is the last date of application submission for the respective centre.
  • SSLC/SSC/ISC mark sheet/certificate, or any other valid document, is accepted as proof of date of birth.
  • The EWS certificate must strictly follow the DoPT-prescribed format (available at www.persmin.nic.in); the OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate must also be in the prescribed format.

Selection Process

  1. Initial screening based on academic records and other parameters declared in the online application; only screened-in candidates proceed further.
  2. C-DAC may raise the minimum eligibility criteria/cut-offs at its discretion if the number of applicants is high for any post.
  3. Candidates are evaluated on academic credentials, experience profile, written test marks (if applicable), and interview performance.
  4. The selection process is carried out independently by each C-DAC centre, based on its own requirements; only shortlisted candidates are contacted.
  5. All submitted information is verified against original documents at document verification or any later stage; false or non-conforming information leads to rejection/cancellation at any stage.
Note: Mere issue of an interview call letter does not imply acceptance of candidature or selection for the post. No TA/DA is paid for attending a written test or interview.

How to Apply for C-DAC Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit careers.cdac.in and locate the relevant centre's job listing for the JIT October 2026 Cycle.
  2. Read the General Terms and Conditions and confirm your eligibility for the specific post before starting.
  3. Click Apply against the position you wish to apply for, and log in using your mobile number and the OTP received.
  4. Fill in the application form (returning applicants from a previous C-DAC advertisement will see a prefilled, editable form).
  5. Upload a scanned photograph (JPG, max 400 KB) and your resume (PDF, max 500 KB).
  6. Review the prefilled details, add any additional information, and click Submit.
  7. Note the unique application number generated by the system, and print the application form for your records.
Important: Candidates applying for multiple posts must submit a separate application for each post. No hard copy/printed application should be sent to C-DAC. Government/PSU/Autonomous Body employees should apply online and also route a signed printout through proper channel, or carry a No Objection Certificate (NOC) to the interview.

Important Conditions

  • No application fee is charged by C-DAC for this advertisement.
  • Selected candidates are engaged purely on contract and derive no right or claim to a regular post/appointment in C-DAC.
  • A selected candidate may be deputed or transferred to any C-DAC project location across India, based on organizational requirement.
  • Interview call letters and all correspondence are sent only by email, to the address provided in the online application; no hard copies are sent.
  • Internal candidates, if finally selected, must resign from their current C-DAC service and join the new post as a fresh employee.
  • C-DAC reserves the right to increase, decrease, or not fill any notified post, and to cancel/restrict/curtail/enlarge the recruitment process, without prior notice or reason.
  • Canvassing in any form leads to disqualification.
  • In case of any ambiguity between language versions, the English version prevails.
  • C-DAC has not authorized any agent/agency to represent it for recruitment matters; all official queries go through the respective centre's HR/Recruitment Team.

The selection is based on performance in Stage-I, Stage-II, Stage-III and Stage-IV, meeting the laid down medical standards during medical examination and the number of vacancies available for the post in the respective batch. Qualification in Stage-I, II, III and IV is compulsory for recruitment in ICG.

  • Selection of candidates for the post of Yantrik will be only for CGEPT-01/27, and for Navik (DB) and Hygienist-I only for CGEPT-02/27.
  • Selection of candidates for the post of Navik (GD) in either CGEPT-01/27 or CGEPT-02/27 batch will be based on order of merit, available vacancies and administrative requirement. Candidates cannot claim their selection in a particular batch.
  • All candidates will be compulsorily subjected to identity check prior to commencement of the examination at Stage-I, II and III of CGEPT. The identity check includes verification/matching at all stages of the selection procedure.

Live Image Capture and Biometric

  • The candidate has to upload the latest photograph during registration. A live image of the candidate will also be captured during registration, and its facial features will be matched against the uploaded photograph and the real-time photo captured during the online application. The photograph in the application form will be matched with facial features and physical appearance of the candidate at all subsequent stages.
  • Only left thumb biometric will be captured at the Stage-I recruitment centre before the online exam. If the biometric of the left thumb is not captured during Stage-I, then the biometric of the right thumb will be captured and used for subsequent verification. Apart from left and right thumb, no other finger will be considered for biometric.
  • It is the candidate’s responsibility to check beforehand that the biometric machines are able to capture the fingerprint image. Due to Mehndi, wax, etc., if the biometric machine is not able to capture the fingerprint image, the candidate will not be allowed to appear in the examination.
  • Failure in even one of the identity checks at any stage will lead to cancellation of candidature.

Stage-I: Computer Based Online Examination

  • A Computer Based Examination (CBE) with a total of 100 questions, each carrying 01 mark, will be conducted. The question paper will be bilingual (Hindi and English) and objective type (Multiple Choice Questions). Duration of the examination is one hour. There is no negative marking for wrong answers. The detailed syllabus is available at www.ssc.gov.in.
  • Candidates will be required to bring the following documents at the reporting centre: valid original identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport) as submitted/uploaded in the online application; one printout of E-admit card (B&W printout of E-admit card will be accepted provided the candidate’s photograph, QR codes and all other details are clearly visible/legible); and two in no. passport size colour photographs as uploaded in the online application.
  • If the exam is conducted in multiple shifts, marks scored will be normalised and these normalised scores will be used to determine final merit and cut-off marks.
  • The result of Stage-I will be uploaded on the candidate’s dashboard on www.ssc.gov.in.
Ser. No. Category Passing Marks
1 UR/EWS/OBC 40
2 SC/ST 35

Stage-II: Recruitment Process at Recruitment Centres

Stage-II is held at Recruitment Centres specified by ICG. Based on performance in the Computer Based Online Examination and the handling capacity of ICG Recruitment Centres, candidates will be shortlisted for Stage-II, and an E-admit card will be issued. Stage-II of candidates shortlisted for CGEPT-01/27 and CGEPT-02/27 batches will be held conjointly. To download E-admit cards, candidates are required to upload additional documents as mentioned in para 7.5 and select a preferred date and centre in a given period. Failure to upload additional documents or submit date/centre choice within the time frame promulgated by ICG will lead to cancellation of candidature. Allocation of date and centre for Stage-II exams will be on “first come first serve” basis. Candidates will be given the option to select date and centre; date and centre where seats are available will be shown to the candidates for selection. The duration of Stage-II is 1-2 days and it involves the following examination, which are only qualifying in nature:

  • Basic Identity and Biometric Verification: All candidates reporting for Stage-II will be allowed to enter ICG recruitment centres post basic identity check at the entrance gate and further subjected to biometric verification. Candidates whose identity cannot be verified at the entrance gate will not be allowed to enter ICG recruitment centres and will be disqualified from the recruitment process.
  • Physical Fitness Test (PFT): Candidates undergoing PFT will do so at their own risk. All candidates are advised to be in possession of sports rig (Shoe, T-shirt, Trouser etc.). All four tests of PFT are carried out in continuity without any break. Any break in these tests will lead to failure in PFT.
  • Assessment and Adaptability Test: Candidates qualified in PFT will undergo an online/OMR based examination to qualify for further stages of Stage-II recruitment process. This test is qualifying in nature and the marks obtained will not be included in the final merit list. The result will be announced at the venue after the conduct of the examination.
  • Document Verification: All information provided in the online application has to match with all original documents produced by the candidate such as Class 10th/Class 12th/Diploma marksheet, identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport/Domicile/category certificate), individual subject and aggregate marks/CGPA (as applicable). The candidates will be declared either Pass or Fail in document verification. Any mismatch, inconsistency or error with the information provided in the application form, uploaded document and original documents produced for verification at Stage-II will lead to rejection in document verification. The date of issue of all documents has to be on or before the closing date of application. The validity of all uploaded documents has to be at least up to 31 December 2027. Any false declaration in the online application will lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • Recruitment Medical Examination: The Recruitment Medical Officer will assess the candidates for medical fitness as per laid down medical standards and declare them fit or unfit. Candidates who have qualified document verification will be subjected to recruitment medical examination. Candidates found medically unfit in the Recruitment Medical Examination and who wish to appeal will be immediately referred to the designated military hospital (allocated by ICG). The candidates are to report to the designated AFMS hospital within 14 days of completion of Recruitment Medical Examination. The appeal medical examination will be considered as final and the candidate will have no right for further appeal at any other or same hospital again.

1 Male 06 min 30 sec 20 15 15

Candidates declared fit in the recruitment medical examination at Stage-II recruitment centre may be disqualified in document verification during the further scrutiny of the documents by ICG, as document verification is carried out at multiple stages even after the conduct of Stage-II and prior to publishing the final merit/result.

Final Merit List for Stage-III

The merit list (zone-wise and category-wise) for Navik (GD) male and all India (category-wise) for Navik (GD) female, Yantriks, Navik (DB) and Hygienist-I will be prepared for candidates who have qualified all the Stages and meeting the requisite criteria as mentioned in the advertisement. Shortlisting of candidates for the post of Navik (GD) in either CGEPT-01/27 or CGEPT-02/27 batch will be based on order of merit and available vacancies. The candidates’ order of merit will only be based on marks scored in Stage-I, qualification in all phases of Stage-II and number of available vacancies. Assessment test marks shall not form part of the final merit but shall be used only for breaking a tie. The tie-breaking rule in merit, in case of two or more candidates having the same marks in Stage-I, is as follows (wherever tie is broken next stage will not be proceeded):

  1. Candidate older in age will be higher in merit.
  2. Candidate scoring more marks in the Assessment Test.

Stage-III: INS Chilka

Candidates who qualify Stage-I and Stage-II and stand in merit as per the vacancies available will be provisionally shortlisted for reporting at INS Chilka and will be issued a provisional E-admit card. Stage-III will be conducted separately for each cadre in the respective batch, i.e. Navik (GD) and Yantriks in CGEPT-01/27 and Navik (GD), Navik (DB) and Hygienist-I in CGEPT-02/27 batch. The duration of Stage-III is 1-2 days. INS Chilka is a Naval training establishment; verification procedure at training base is in vogue applicable for ICG candidates. Stage-III involves the following:

  • Basic Identity Check: All candidates reporting for Stage-III recruitment at INS Chilka will be subjected to Aadhaar based identity verification. Changes made in demographic details (Name, date of birth, physical appearance) in the Aadhaar during the last two years will be scrutinised. In case of any discrepancy or mismatch, candidates must submit valid supporting documents; bonafide changes may be considered upon submission of an affidavit. In case of suspected fraud or absence of valid proof, the candidate shall be liable for cancellation.
  • Document Verification: All information provided in the online application has to match with all original documents produced by the candidate. Any mismatch, inconsistency or error will lead to rejection in document verification and the candidature will be cancelled.
  • Pre-Enrolment Medicals: The pre-enrolment medical examination of all selected candidates will be done by the Recruitment Medical Officer at INS Chilka. The conduct of pre-enrolment medical examination will depend on the time gap between recruitment medical examination conducted during Stage-II and date of reporting of candidates at INS Chilka. Candidates who are found medically unfit and who wish to appeal will be immediately referred to a designated military hospital (either INHS Nivarini or INHS Kalyani) as allocated by medical authorities at INS Chilka. Such candidates are to report to the designated Military Hospitals and complete the appeal medicals within a maximum period of five working days as part of the appeal medical examination. The appeal medical examination will be considered as final and the candidate will have no right for further appeal at any other or same hospital again.
  • Submission of Documents: All candidates are to submit original documents, police verification forms and other associated forms along with the E-admit card at Stage-III. Candidates should be in possession of police verification from either place of domicile or place of present residence, which should have been obtained after last date of submission of application form. Candidates without verified police verification reports or reports with adverse comments will not be eligible for enrolment.

Stage-IV: Training Base

Stage-IV shall comprise verification/authentication of original educational and other documents submitted during Stage-III with the concerned Boards/Universities/State Government authorities. A candidate will be terminated from service if documents are reported as not genuine by the respective Boards/Universities/State Government.

ICG CGEPT Medical and Physical Standards

The medical examination is conducted by authorised Medical Officers of Defence Forces as per the medical standard prescribed in current regulations applicable to Enrolled Persons on entry.

Parameter Standard as per notification
Height Minimum height standard for male candidates is 157 cms and for female candidates is 152 cms. Height standards may be reduced by up to 05 cms for candidates having domicile of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Garhwal, Kumaon and Sikkim. Relaxation of 05 cms is also applicable to Gorkhas. Height standards may be reduced by up to 02 cms for candidates having domicile of Ladakh, Lakshadweep & Minicoy Islands and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
Chest Chest wall should be well proportioned and well developed. Minimum chest circumference for male candidates should be 77 cm with chest expansion of at least 05 cm. For female candidates, the chest should be well proportioned with minimum expansion of 05 cm.
Weight Proportionate to height and age as applicable for ICG.
Hearing The candidate should have normal hearing, i.e. able to hear focused whisper from a distance of 06 m by each ear separately.
Tattoo Permanent body tattoos are not permitted on any part of the body. However, certain concessions are permitted to candidates belonging to tribal areas communities as declared by the Govt. of India. For other candidates, permanent body tattoos are only permitted on inner face of forearms i.e. from inside of elbow to the wrist and on reverse side of palm/back (dorsal) side of hand.
Dental Should have healthy gums, good set of teeth and minimum 14 dental points.
General Health Candidate should be fit for the Armed forces, must conform to the medical standards, have normal anatomy without loss or deformity of any appendages, and be free from any active or latent, acute or chronic, medical or surgical disability or communicable disease, infection and skin ailments. Candidate shall be physically and mentally fit to perform duty in any part of the world, in any climate and terrain places.
Gender Any candidate if found to have predominant characteristics of the opposite gender as evident on external physical examination will be rejected as unfit. Any candidate having undergone gender reassignment surgery will be declared unfit.
Pregnancy (female candidates only) Any candidate, if found to be pregnant shall be disqualified and her candidature will be rejected.
Gynaecological Examination (female candidates only) The examination covers external genitalia, hernia orifices and the perineum. Any evidence of stress urinary incontinence or genital prolapse outside introitus shall lead to disqualification of the candidate.
Branch Standard
General Duty Branch 6/6 (Better eye) and 6/9 (Worse eye)
Domestic Branch 6/36 (Better eye) and 6/36 (Worse eye)
Technical Branch (Yantriks) 6/24 (Better eye) and 6/24 (Worse eye)
Hygienist 6/60 (Better) and 6/60 (Worse) without glasses; 6/9 (Better) and 6/24 (Worse) with glasses
  • Candidates using glasses are not eligible for GD Branch.
  • Candidates are advised to get their ears cleaned for wax and tartar removed from teeth prior to medical examination.
  • Candidates claiming height relaxation are to submit a domicile certificate to the medical officer. Failure to submit the domicile certificate will lead to non-waiver of height relaxation.
  • No waiver will be given for laid down medical standards. The Indian Coast Guard (ICG) order on medical standard will be the final authority.

How to Apply for ICG CGEPT Recruitment 2026

Applications will be accepted online from 06 October 2026 (1100 hrs) to 21 October 2026 (1730 hrs). Candidates have to log in to www.ssc.gov.in and follow the instructions for registering themselves.

  1. Visit www.ssc.gov.in and follow the instructions for registration. Remember the registered E-mail ID and mobile number, as the same would be encrypted in the application form. If the candidate forgets the E-mail ID or mobile number, it would not be possible to log in to the candidate’s dashboard, and neither would he/she be able to download E-admit card or see his/her result. ICG would not be responsible for this.
  2. Abide by the guidelines for filling the application form as mentioned on the registration portal and by the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) available on www.ssc.gov.in.
  3. Apply for only one post. If a candidate fills multiple applications during a particular recruitment cycle, only the latest filled application submitted by the candidate shall be considered and all previously filled applications will be rejected. However, the examination fees for multiple applications filled will not be refunded.
  4. Upload the compulsory documents listed below, in the specified format.
  5. Pay the examination fee online (except SC/ST candidates, who are exempted).
  6. Use the print preview option before the final submission of the online application to check that all details (such as Name, Date of Birth, Parent’s name, subject wise marks/CGPA, validity date of documents and category certificate details) are correct.
  7. Candidates will also be provided with an edit/correction window for a duration of 02-03 days to edit/correct only a few fields in the online application. Candidates are to use the edit window when provided to correct mistakes made while filling the online application.

For any query regarding online application, the candidate can contact through e-mail at [email protected] and telephone number 7620207872.

ICG CGEPT Apply Online: Compulsory Documents at the Time of Application

  • Passport size recent colour photograph (should not be older than three months prior to the date of opening of application) as per the specifications mentioned on the registration portal.
  • Live image of the candidate, captured during registration.
  • Candidate’s scanned signature image.
  • Date of Birth proof (Class 10th marksheet OR Birth Certificate).
  • Identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport).
  • Service Certificate/NOC if the candidate is serving ICG Personnel or civilian.
  • A valid Domicile Certificate to determine the zone of candidate for zone-wise recruitment for all candidates applying for the post of Navik (GD) male. In states where both certificates, i.e. Domicile and Resident certificates, are issued, only the Domicile Certificate will be accepted.
  • Candidates applying for the post of Navik (GD) female, Yantriks, Navik (DB) and Hygienist-I are required to upload a domicile certificate only if they require relaxations in medical standards viz. height.

Only scanned copies of the original documents shall be uploaded; photocopies or self-attested photocopies shall not be accepted. All documents uploaded must be in Hindi or English; if a document is in any other language, both original and English translation must be uploaded. Applications with blurred photograph, signature and uploaded documents will be rejected during document verification. The complete document is to be scanned and uploaded (e.g. if a Date of Birth Certificate or Category Certificate or Identity proof has two or more pages, then all the pages are to be merged in one file and uploaded in the online application).

Documents to be Uploaded if Shortlisted for Stage-II

  • All candidates: Category Certificate (SC/ST/OBC (Non-Creamy layer)/EWS); NOC from Government Organisation if the candidate is employed (NOC should be dated on or after the date of publication of the advertisement).
  • Hygienist-I (in addition): Class 8th marksheet; Class 10th marksheet (if completed); Class 10th certificate (if completed); ITI certificate and marksheet.
  • Navik (DB) (in addition): Class 10th marksheet; Class 10th certificate; additional marksheet of Class 10th (if applicable).
  • Navik (GD) (in addition to the Navik (DB) documents): Class 12th marksheet; Class 12th certificate; additional marksheet of Class 12th (if applicable).
  • Yantrik (in addition to the above): Class 12th marksheet (if completed); Class 12th certificate (if completed); marksheet of all years/semesters of diploma; Diploma Passing Certificate; additional mark sheet of Class 12th/Diploma (if applicable).

SC/ST/OBC (Non-Creamy Layer)/EWS applicants availing their respective quota must have the address in the category certificate the same as the current or permanent address mentioned in the online application. The EWS certificate shall be as per Govt. of India format. The OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate should bear QR/bar code for appointment under post under the Govt. of India and should specifically mention that the candidate does not belong to person/sections (Creamy Layer) as mentioned in relevant government orders. Additionally, OBC candidates must produce a valid and latest OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate.

ICG CGEPT Documents Required at Each Stage

Stage Documents
Stage-I Valid original identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport) as submitted/uploaded in the online application; one printout of E-admit card (B&W printout accepted if photograph and all other details are clearly visible/legible); two in no. passport size colour photographs as uploaded in the online application with similar facial features.
Stage-II Printout of “Online application and E-admit card of Stage-I and Stage-II” (B&W printout accepted if photograph and all other details are clearly visible); identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport) as submitted/uploaded in the online application; original documents submitted/uploaded in the online application form and candidates login after being shortlisted for Stage-II; 02 photocopies of all original documents duly self-attested; 12 passport size colour photographs, same as submitted in online application with similar facial features; Service certificate/NOC for ICG in original and 02 self-attested photocopies from the employer for candidates presently serving in any government organisation or PSU (if applicable). For SC/ST candidates only: additional one printout of E-admit card, original category certificate and two photocopies of self-attested SC/ST certificate, original train/bus ticket, cancelled cheque leaf for NEFT payment and travel form downloaded from website for claiming TA. No fare for taxi or any other conveyance will be permitted.
Stage-III Printout of “Online application and Stage-III E-admit card” (printout will be accepted provided the candidate’s photograph and all other details are clearly visible/legible); original of the documents submitted/uploaded in online application form and candidate’s login after being shortlisted for Stage-III; 03 photocopies of all original documents duly self-attested; 30 passport size colour photographs; 10 colour photographs measuring 3.5 cms x 2.5 cms with blue background; parental willingness certificate (one copy original and 02 Xerox copies); police verification certificate (one copy original and 02 Xerox copies); family particular certificate (one copy original and 02 Xerox copies); character certificate (one copy original and 02 Xerox copies); willingness certificate (one copy original and 02 Xerox copies); attestation form (with cadre name) (03 copies original); NOC in original with four self-attested photocopies along with vigilance clearance certificate from the employer for candidates presently serving in any government organisation or public sector undertaking (on confirmation of induction, discharge certificate is to be provided prior to commencement of training); identity proof (Aadhaar Card OR PAN Card OR Voter ID card OR Driving License OR Passport) as submitted/uploaded in the online application.

Aadhaar Card and mobile number linked with Aadhaar Card is mandatory at Stage-III for opening of bank account and generation of Permanent Retirement Account Number.

Training: Basic training for CGEPT-01/2027 will commence in May 2027 and for CGEPT-02/2027 in November 2027 at INS Chilka, followed by sea training and professional training in allotted trade. Branch/trade will be allocated as per requirement of service and performance during basic training. Candidates are liable to be discharged as UNSUITABLE if their progress (including academic) or conduct is unsatisfactory at any time during training. Further, at any stage of training or service, if the online application or any document furnished by the individual is found to be falsified, the individual shall be liable to be discharged from ICG service.

ICG CGEPT Important Instructions

  • Candidates withdrawn on disciplinary grounds from any other or Government service training establishments are not eligible to appear.
  • Candidates who have been arrested, convicted or against whom criminal proceedings, investigation, enquiry or trial is pending before any court or law enforcement agency shall disclose full details of the same in the application form and at the time of document verification. Suppression or concealment of any such information shall render the candidate liable to cancellation at any stage of the recruitment process.
  • A candidate who is arrested, convicted or against whom an FIR is registered or criminal proceedings are initiated during the recruitment process shall immediately inform the Indian Coast Guard through the prescribed channel.
  • All original certificates and marksheets produced at the time of Stage-II will be returned to the candidate post verification. All original certificates and marksheets produced at the time of Stage-III will be retained by ICG if cleared Stage-IV or returned to the candidate post verification if declared fail.
  • The candidate’s selection pertaining to a particular batch is valid for that batch only. Qualified candidates whose names do not appear in the final merit list cannot claim admission for the next batch. These candidates will have to undergo the selection procedure afresh provided that they meet the eligibility criteria for fresh selection.
  • Applications received by post will not be accepted.
  • E-admit card for Stage-III will be forwarded only to candidates qualifying Stage-II and standing in merit as per vacancies. Such candidates will be required to reach the training establishment, i.e. INS Chilka, at their own expense on the date given on their Stage-III E-admit card. Late reporting on any ground will not be accepted.
  • No enquiry will be entertained regarding recruitment/enrolment for this batch after 31 December 2027.
  • Indiscipline activities including copying/malpractice etc. during the testing procedures will also result in disqualification. The decision of ICG will be final and binding on all candidates with regard to copying/malpractice.
  • No candidate should misbehave in any manner or create disorderly scene in examination premises. Candidates found impersonating or misbehaving will be debarred from appearing in current and future examinations of ICG.
  • Use of Mobile phones and other electronic gadgets of any kind are not permitted during examination. If any candidate is caught with Mobile, Bluetooth device, any kind of recording/scanning/hearing/capturing equipment etc. during Stage I, II and III then his candidature will be cancelled and immediately action as per law including filing of FIR will be initiated.
  • Candidates must have valid e-mail ID and mobile number for successful online registration. The communication by ICG with candidates will be only through e-mail or SMS. Candidates are directed to check their login ID and registered e-mail regularly for any change in recruitment schedule.
  • The date of birth and gender will not be allowed to be changed at any subsequent stage under any circumstances whatsoever, and the candidature will be cancelled at any stage wherever any wrong information is detected.
  • Candidates are directed to fill the category details (SC/ST/OBC (Non-Creamy)/EWS) as applicable with due care as no changes are allowed after submission of the application. Candidates declaring the category wrongly in the application form will not be permitted to appear as general candidates.
  • Candidates are strongly advised to apply well in time without waiting for the last date for submission of the online application form.
  • Indian Coast Guard does not assume any responsibility for candidates not being able to submit their applications within the last date or on account of any other reason.
  • The corrigendum, if any, issued on the above advertisement, will be published only on www.ssc.gov.in and candidates are to regularly visit the website for any corrigendum.
  • Candidates who fraudulently claim SC/ST/OBC (Non-creamy)/EWS status or avail any other non-bonafide benefit will be debarred from the current as well as future examinations conducted by ICG.
  • Indian Coast Guard reserves the right to cancel the examination at one centre and shift the examination to another date and centre, and to cancel any test, any stage or the entire recruitment process of this batch without assigning any reason.
  • Persons with any kind of disability are not eligible to apply for ICG as an Armed Force under the Ministry of Defence.
  • Candidates will not be allowed to enter into or contract marriage/keep family with them during the training period.

This is an indicative advertisement. Candidates should see www.ssc.gov.in for the Hindi version of the advertisement and complete update. Only the English advertisement will be referred to in any court of law and not the Hindi version. English version prevails over Hindi advertisement at all times.

Caution: Selection in Indian Coast Guard is fair and on merit basis. Candidates should not fall prey to unscrupulous persons posing as recruitment agents. For complaint against such persons, candidates must approach the Director (Recruitment), Coast Guard Headquarters, Recruitment Center, Noida on telephone 0120-2201340.

Disclaimer (as stated in the notification): The terms and conditions given in the advertisement are guidelines only and orders issued by the Government as amended from time to time will apply during the recruitment process.

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Important Dates

The online application window is open from 06/10/2026 to 26/10/2026. The application form is available on the official website from 10:00 hrs on 06/10/2026 till 17:00 hrs on 26/10/2026. Applications received after the due date will be summarily rejected.

Event Date
Opening Date for Online Applications 06/10/2026 (from 10:00 hrs)
Last Date for Online Applications 26/10/2026 (up to 17:00 hrs)
Queries Accepted Under 'Contact Us' 06/10/2026 (from 11:00 hrs) to 26/10/2026 (up to 13:00 hrs)
Age Calculation Date 26/10/2026
Virtual Interview Date Not Yet Announced
Date of Notification Release Not Available Officially

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Eligibility Criteria

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern eligibility covers nationality, qualification and age. Candidates should read the criteria carefully and confirm they meet every condition before applying, because candidature can be cancelled at any stage if a candidate is found ineligible.

  • Only Indian nationals are eligible to apply.
  • The candidate must have passed the Inter CA or Inter CMA examination.
  • The candidate must be within the prescribed age limit as on 26/10/2026.
  • Applicants without final marks will not be considered and need not apply.

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Qualification

The internship is offered to candidates who have passed Inter CA or Inter CMA and are to be trained in the field of Finance and Accounts. The notification states that eligibility for practical training at NPCIL Units and HQ will be as per the terms and conditions provided by the respective institutions. The notification also states that these prescribed qualifications are the minimum and that possessing them does not entitle a candidate to be called for the interview.

Post Qualification
CA/CMA Intern Passed Inter CA or Inter CMA, subject to the terms and conditions of the respective institutions

Candidates must enter the exact percentage of marks in the qualification section of the form. Marks must not be rounded off, so 49.99% should not be entered as 50%.

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Age Limit

The age limit is calculated as on 26/10/2026. The minimum age is 18 years and the maximum age is 56 years, as printed in the notification. Age relaxation details are not specified in the notification.

Post Minimum Age Maximum Age Not Born On or After Not Born Before
CA/CMA Intern 18 years 56 years 27/10/2008 26/10/1970

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Application Fee

There is no fee for applying for the NPCIL CA/CMA Intern internship. Candidates of all categories can apply online without paying any application fee.

Category Application Fee
All candidates No fee

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Stipend (Salary)

Selected interns receive a monthly stipend rather than a salary, because the notification treats them as trainees. The stipend is Rs 20,000 per month. An additional Rs 5,000 per month is paid where accommodation is not available at the NPCIL Unit or HQ.

Particular Details
Monthly Stipend Rs 20,000 per month
Additional Amount Rs 5,000 per month if accommodation is not available at the Unit/HQ
Tenure 12 months
Extension Up to a further period not exceeding 12 months, case to case, subject to institute requirements and performance of the student

Facilities and Training Conditions

  • Accommodation: A suitable accommodation (single room or bare minimum accommodation) is provided at Units on payment of the normal license fee. If accommodation is not available at Units and HQ, Rs 5,000 per month is given in lieu of accommodation.
  • Transport and medical: Free site transportation subject to availability, and free OPD and first aid facility only.
  • Leave: 1 day of paid leave per month, which is 12 days for one year. For extensions, leave is pro-rata for the extended period. Stipend is deducted proportionately for absence other than admissible leave.
  • Working hours: 8 hours a day in general shift including a 1 hour lunch break, 5 days a week.
  • Injury compensation: NPCIL is liable to pay compensation for personal injury caused by accident arising out of and during training, as per the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923.
  • Status: Interns are treated as trainees and labour-related laws applicable to employees do not apply to them. NPCIL is not obliged to offer employment after the training period.

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Selection Process

The selection is based on Inter CA/Inter CMA marks followed by a virtual personal interview. Screening is done on the aggregate of marks, so only screened-in candidates are informed by e-mail about the further selection process.

  1. Screening: Candidates are shortlisted for the personal interview in the ratio of 1:5, based on the aggregate marks obtained in the Inter CA/Inter CMA examination.
  2. Personal Interview: Selection of interns is by personal interview, which candidates can attend in virtual mode at the respective Unit/Region.
  3. Certificate Verification and Medical Examination: Candidates are engaged after qualifying the standard medical examination and after satisfactory verification of certificates.
  4. Police and Character Verification: Interns are engaged based on the police verification certificate issued by District Police authorities, and a character/conduct certificate must be submitted from the concerned institution.

Tie-Breaking Criteria

  • Candidates with higher marks in the Inter CA/Inter CMA examination are placed higher in the merit list.
  • If both interview marks and Inter CA/Inter CMA marks are equal, the candidate senior in age is ranked higher.
  • If interview marks, Inter CA/Inter CMA marks and age are all the same, the merit list is prepared in alphabetical order of the name (first name, middle name and surname).

Waitlist

The waitlist is limited to the same number of candidates as the main select list and is valid for one year from the date of approval of the panel. It is operated only when a vacancy arises because a selected candidate does not join within the allowed time, or joins but resigns or dies within one year of joining, and a fresh panel is not available by then. It is not operated beyond one year from panel approval or after a new advertisement is notified, whichever is earlier.

Multiple Location Preference

Candidates who wish to apply for more than one location must mention their preference. They are shortlisted on CA/CMA marks only and are interviewed at one of the sites of their choice.

How to Apply for NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Recruitment 2026

NPCIL accepts applications only through its online registration system. Hard copy, handwritten or typed applications delivered in person or by any other means will not be entertained, and candidates should not send any documents or applications to NPCIL.

NPCIL CA/CMA Intern Apply Online

The online application form is available at www.npcilcareers.co.in from 06/10/2026 (10:00 hrs) to 26/10/2026 (17:00 hrs). The online process has four steps: registration, activation, filling details with photo and signature upload, and printing the application form.

  1. Visit the official website www.npcilcareers.co.in.
  2. Click on Apply, then Online Registration, at the top or left corner of the page. Enter basic details such as name, date of birth, category, email and mobile number. An activation link is sent to the email.
  3. Click the activation link received by email to activate the account.
  4. Log in with the Login ID and password. Fill in the stages in order: Educational Qualification, Personal Details, Upload Photo and Signature, and Submit Application. Use the Save and Proceed to Next Step option at each stage.
  5. Check the draft of all entered details at the Submit Application stage. Details can be modified until submission, but no changes are allowed after the application is submitted.
  6. Submit the application to receive the application number, which is also sent by email. View and print the online application form.

Candidates should note their Login ID and password, as these are needed to check the application status through the Applicant's Login link.

Photograph and Signature Requirements

Document Format Size Dimensions
Photograph JPEG Minimum 10 KB, maximum 50 KB Minimum 180 x 240 pixels, maximum 480 x 640 pixels
Signature JPEG Maximum 20 KB Minimum 80 x 100 pixels, maximum 160 x 560 pixels (as printed in the notification)

The uploaded photograph is printed on the call letter, and only the applicant whose photograph is printed on the call letter is allowed to appear for the online interview, certificate verification and medical examination. An application without a valid photograph and signature will not be accepted.

Information to Keep Ready

  • Qualification details and exact percentage of marks
  • Experience details, if any
  • A valid and active email address and contact mobile number, both of which should stay active for at least one year
  • Address for correspondence
  • Scanned photograph and signature in JPEG format

The email ID cannot be changed once entered, and all future correspondence is sent to the registered email. The category (SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/EWS/PwBD) filled in the form cannot be changed later. If a candidate submits multiple applications, only the latest application is considered.

Documents Required for Interview, Certificate Verification and Medical Examination

Shortlisted candidates should keep their Aadhaar Card and online application form ready when reporting for the online interview, and must carry a clearly printed e-Call Letter. Original documents and self-attested copies, along with a duly signed hard copy of the online application, are required at certificate verification and medical examination. Candidates who do not produce the required documents will not be allowed to appear for the medical examination.

  • SC/ST/OBC (Non Creamy Layer): Caste/category certificate in the format prescribed by the Government of India. OBC (NCL) certificates must be issued on or after 01/04/2026, and OBC applicants called for the interview must give an undertaking at the time of reporting that they belong to the OBC (Non Creamy Layer) category.
  • EWS: Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed format from a competent authority, valid for the year 2026-27.
  • PwBD: Disability certificate issued by an authority prescribed in the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017.
  • Certificates in other languages: A self-certified translated copy in English or Hindi if a certificate is issued in any other language.
  • Police verification certificate issued by District Police authorities and a character/conduct certificate from the concerned institution.

The prescribed format for the EWS certificate can be downloaded from www.npcilcareers.co.in, and the standard formats enclosed with the notification are for SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/EWS/PwBD and the OBC undertaking.

Other Important Conditions

  • NPCIL reserves the right to fill all intern vacancies, alter the number of vacancies, or cancel, suspend, postpone or alter the whole recruitment process, and to change the recruitment criteria at any stage without prior notice.
  • Issue of an e-Call Letter for the virtual interview gives no right or claim to the internship. Final selection is based on merit and subject to all eligibility conditions and Government of India guidelines on reservation and concessions.
  • No request for change of the virtual interview date or time will be entertained.
  • A candidate who provides wrong information, submits false documents, suppresses relevant information, uses unfair means, is found guilty of impersonation or uploads a non-human or irrelevant photograph is liable to be disqualified, prosecuted and debarred, and the application or appointment is cancelled.
  • Records of candidates who are not selected are not preserved beyond 6 months from the date of publication of the select list.
  • In case of any ambiguity arising from versions other than English, the English version prevails. Legal jurisdiction for any dispute is Mumbai.
  • NPCIL strives to have a workforce which reflects gender balance and women applicants are encouraged to apply.

  • Application mode: Online only, through www.sci.gov.in
  • Pay Level: Level 6 of Pay Matrix, initial Basic Pay of Rs. 35,400/- plus allowances

SCI Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026 Overview

The Supreme Court of India invites online applications from Indian citizens who fulfil the prescribed qualifications and eligibility conditions, as on 1st September 2026, for selection of suitable candidates for preparation of a panel for filling up 250 tentative vacancies of Junior Court Assistant. The number of posts may be subject to change due to administrative exigencies and/or the requirement of the Registry.

Particulars Details
Organization Supreme Court of India (SCI)
Advertisement No. F.6/2026-SC (RC)
Advertisement Date September 30, 2026
Post Name Junior Court Assistant
Post Category Group-B Non-Gazetted
Total Vacancies 250 (tentative)
Pay Level Level 6 of Pay Matrix, initial Basic Pay Rs. 35,400/- plus allowances
Application Mode Online

SCI Junior Court Assistant Important Dates

Candidates applying for SCI Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026 must note the following timeline carefully.

Event Date
Starting date for online registration 7th October 2026
SCI Junior Court Assistant Last Date to apply online 28th October 2026, till 11:55 p.m.
Crucial date for determining eligibility (age, qualification) 1st September 2026
Objective Type Test (tentative) 20th November 2026
Uploading of Answer Keys 22nd November 2026
Objection window on Answer Keys (tentative) 22nd November 2026 to 23rd November 2026, till 11:55 p.m.
Typing Speed Test, Written Test (Descriptive), and Interview Dates to be notified on www.sci.gov.in

SCI Junior Court Assistant Vacancy 2026 Details

A total of 250 tentative vacancies have been announced for the post of Junior Court Assistant. The number of posts may be subject to change due to administrative exigencies and/or the requirement of the Registry, which reserves the right to effect such change with the approval of the Competent Authority.

The benefit of reservation will be in accordance with Rule 4A of the Supreme Court Officers and Servants (Conditions of Service and Conduct) Rules, 1961.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Eligibility Criteria 2026

SCI Junior Court Assistant eligibility 2026 is based on educational qualification and computer typing proficiency, along with the prescribed age limit, as on 1st September 2026.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Qualification

  • Bachelor's degree of a recognized University in India.
  • Knowledge of Computer operation, with a typing speed of 35 w.p.m. on computer.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Age Limit 2026

As on 1st September 2026, candidates should not be below 18 years of age. The upper age limit for candidates is 30 years.

  • Usual age relaxation is admissible to candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer), Physically Challenged, and Ex-Servicemen, as per Government of India Rules.
  • Relaxation up to a maximum of 5 years, over and above the prescribed age limit of 30 years, is admissible to dependents of freedom fighters.
  • There is no upper age limit for Departmental candidates of the Registry of the Supreme Court of India.
  • No relaxation in age will be allowed to candidates working in other Government Departments/Public Sector Undertakings/Nationalized Banks, etc.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Salary 2026

Selected candidates for the post of Junior Court Assistant will be placed in Level 6 of the Pay Matrix, with an initial Basic Pay of Rs. 35,400/- plus allowances, as admissible under the rules of the Supreme Court of India.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Application Fee 2026

Eligible candidates are required to apply online for which a link will be provided through the website of the Supreme Court of India, www.sci.gov.in. The application will be accepted through online registration only; no postal application form shall be accepted.

Category Application Fee (Non-Refundable)
General/Unreserved Rs. 1,500/- plus Bank charges
SC/ST/OBC (Non-Creamy Layer)/Ex-Servicemen/Physically Challenged Rs. 750/- plus Bank charges

Fee must be paid through online mode only, via the payment gateway provided by UCO Bank. Fee shall not be accepted in any other form, and once paid, will not be refunded under any circumstances or in any eventuality.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Selection Process 2026

Eligible candidates are required to appear in the following stages of examination for selection to the post of Junior Court Assistant.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Scheme of Examination

S.No. Details of Test Duration Maximum Marks Minimum Qualifying Marks
1 Objective Type Test (Multiple Choice Questions) – 100 questions: 20 General English (incl. comprehension), 15 General Aptitude, 15 General Knowledge, 15 provisions relating to Judiciary in the Constitution of India, 10 Supreme Court Rules 2013, 10 Supreme Court Officers and Servants (Conditions of Service and Conduct) Rules 1961, and 15 Computer Knowledge 1½ hours 100 50
2 Typing Speed Test on Computer, in English Language, with minimum speed 35 w.p.m. (mistakes allowed: 3% of total words typed) 10 minutes 50 25
3 Written Test (Descriptive), in English Language — Comprehension passage, Precis Writing, and Essay Writing 2 hours 100 50
4 Interview — 25 13

SCI Junior Court Assistant Shortlisting Ratios

In case a large number of candidates qualify the Objective Type Test by securing the minimum qualifying 50 marks or more, candidates will be shortlisted for the second stage (Typing Speed Test and Written Test) in the ratio of 1:10 against the number of tentative vacancies, based on the merit list.

The Written Test (Descriptive) answer sheets will be evaluated only for candidates who successfully qualify the Typing Speed Test, since qualifying the Typing Speed Test is mandatory. Candidates who successfully qualify all three tests — Objective Type Test, Typing Speed Test, and Written Test — will be shortlisted for Interview in the ratio of 1:3 against the number of tentative vacancies.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Test Centres

The Objective Type Test will be conducted at cities notified in Annexure-A of the official advertisement. The Typing Speed Test and Written Test (Descriptive) will be conducted in Delhi/NCR only. The Interview will be conducted either through online mode or in physical mode in Delhi, as per the directions of the Competent Authority.

There will be negative marking of 0.25 marks for each incorrect answer in the Objective Type Test (Multiple Choice Questions). Candidates may submit objections to the Answer Keys through online mode only, within the notified objection window, on payment of a fee of Rs. 100/- per objection, which will be refunded if the objection is found valid.

How to Apply for SCI Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026

SCI Junior Court Assistant Apply Online process is entirely online, through the link provided on the Supreme Court of India's website.

  1. Visit the official website: www.sci.gov.in and access the online application link provided for the recruitment.
  2. Fill in the online Application Form with accurate personal, educational, and category details. Note that Name, Father's name, Mother's name, and Date of Birth must be entered exactly as per the High School Certificate/Xth Board Examination certificate.
  3. Upload scanned copies of your recent photograph, signature, and requisite documents (Class Xth, Class XIIth, and Graduation Certificates, caste/community certificate for reserved category candidates, and disability certificate, if applicable).
  4. Furnish the required Undertaking confirming that you have read and understood the terms and conditions of the advertisement and will abide by them.
  5. Make payment of the applicable application fee online, through the payment gateway provided by UCO Bank.
  6. Preview the Application Form after successful completion, and take a printout of the filled-up form for your records (this printout need not be sent to the Registry).
  7. Submit the application on or before 28th October 2026, till 11:55 p.m.
  8. Retain your Application Number carefully, for generation of the Admit Card from the link to be provided on the Supreme Court of India website.

SCI Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026 – Important Instructions

  • Admission at all stages of the Examination — Objective Type Test, Typing Speed Test, Written Test (Descriptive), and Interview — will be purely provisional; eligibility documents will be checked/verified at the time of document verification.
  • If a candidate is found guilty of impersonation, submitting fabricated/false documents, or furnishing false information at any stage, they will be removed/disqualified, prosecuted, and debarred from future appointment in the Registry.
  • Application once submitted cannot be withdrawn or modified; candidates should ensure all particulars are correct before final submission.
  • Fee once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances or in any eventuality.
  • In case a candidate submits more than one Application Form, only the form with the latest Application Number, lastly submitted, will be considered; no correspondence requesting acceptance of previous forms will be entertained.
  • No request for change of category filled in the online Application Form will be entertained.
  • Candidates must have a valid personal e-mail ID and mobile number, kept active throughout the recruitment process, as information will be sent via SMS and e-mail.
  • No TA/DA will be payable for appearing in the Tests/Interview. No Admit Cards will be sent by post; candidates must download them from the Supreme Court of India website.
  • Concessions/facilities in the Tests will be extended to Persons with Disabilities as per the Government of India's prescribed Office Memorandum; the facility of a scribe may be availed by PwBD candidates by submitting the proforma at Annexure-I or Annexure-IA, along with the requisite certificate. The scribe's qualification must be a minimum of two academic years below and a maximum of three academic years below the minimum qualification for the post.
  • Candidates working in Central/State Government Departments/Nationalized Banks/Public Sector Undertakings, etc., must submit a 'No Objection Certificate' from their employer at the time of document verification.
  • If a candidate who was unemployed at the time of application gets employment during or after the examination process, they must immediately intimate this to the Branch Officer, Recruitment Cell, at [email protected], failing which adverse inference will be drawn by the Registry.
  • Application forms which do not comply with the instructions shall be summarily rejected.
  • In case of any dispute(s), the jurisdiction will be Delhi.
