How to Download the WBPSC Miscellaneous Answer Key 2026 PDF

The answer key is published on the official WBPSC website. Follow these steps:

  1. Open the official website of the West Bengal Public Service Commission at psc.wb.gov.in.
  2. On the homepage, look under the "What's New" section.
  3. Click the link for downloading the answer key for the Written/Screening Test.
  4. Select the answer key for the WBPSC Miscellaneous Preliminary (Objective Type) Examination 2024, Advt. No. 13/2024.
  5. The provisional answer key PDF will open on your screen.
  6. Find the answers for your own test booklet series (A, B, C or D).
  7. Download and save the PDF for reference.

Also Read: RPSC APO Final Answer Key 2026

Marking Scheme of WBPSC Miscellaneous Prelims

Response Type Marks
Correct Answer +2
Incorrect Answer 0
Unattempted Question 0

How to Calculate Your Marks Using the Answer Key

Compare each answer you marked with the official key. Count only the answers that match, then apply this formula:

Estimated Score = Number of Correct Answers × 2

Example: if a candidate gets 72 answers right, gets 18 wrong and leaves 10 blank, the estimated score is 72 × 2 = 144 out of 200.

This score is only an estimate, because the answer key is provisional and may change after objections are reviewed.

How to Raise an Objection Against the WBPSC Miscellaneous Answer Key

If you believe an answer in the provisional key is wrong, you can challenge it online during the objection window, 06/10/2026 to 08/10/2026.

  1. Visit the official WBPSC website at psc.wb.gov.in.
  2. Open the answer key response or objection link given for the Miscellaneous Preliminary Examination.
  3. Log in with the credentials asked on the portal, such as your roll or enrolment number and password or date of birth.
  4. Select the exam, your test booklet series and the question number you are disputing.
  5. Enter the answer you consider correct.
  6. Attach valid supporting proof or a reference document.
  7. Submit the objection and save the acknowledgement, if one is shown.

Also Read: APPSC Assistant Professor Exam Date 2026

Objection Fee

Whether a fee applies to objections is Not Available Officially in the sources reviewed for this article. Check the official notice on psc.wb.gov.in before you submit.

Proof Required for an Objection

  • A valid document or reference that supports your proposed answer.
  • The correct booklet series and question number.
  • One clear objection per disputed question. Avoid duplicates.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Use only the official WBPSC website to download the key and file objections.
  • Do not wait for the last day. The window closes on 08/10/2026.
  • Check the booklet series before comparing answers.
  • Do not rely on social media posts or unofficial keys as proof.
  • The provisional key can change. Wait for the final answer key before treating any score as confirmed.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

  1. Objection review: WBPSC examines the objections received during the window.
  2. Final answer key: The Commission may publish a final or revised key after the review. The date is Not Yet Announced.
  3. Preliminary result: The result will follow the final key. The date is Not Yet Announced.
  4. Next stage: Qualified candidates move to the next stage as per the official recruitment scheme. Main exam dates are Not Yet Announced.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.
